text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN
- The Central Depository Company may start trial operations by the end of this month after the approval of a set of rules by the Corporate Law Authority.

- Ahmed Sadiq, a former principal secretary to ousted prime minister Benazir Bhutto, two officials of Pakistan International Airlines and six officials of the Civil Aviation Authority have been arrested for alleged irregularities.
- Rangers set up checkposts around Karachi to avert any untoward incident during the forthcoming month of Muharram.
BUSINESS RECORDER
- A spokesman for the Privatisation Commission has denied reported postponement of the privatisation of Pakistan Telecommunication Company Ltd.
- The government has set a deadline of December 1997 for the sale of 26 percent shares of Karachi Electric Supply Corporation to a strategic investor as part of its privatisation.
- Pakistan's foreign currency balances have been holding firm at around $900 million mainly on account of the inflows under the National Debt Retirement Programme.
- Commerce Minister Ishaq Dar rejected the demand of All Pakistan Textile Mills Association on importing cotton from India.
FINANCIAL POST
- An official spokesman said the government may reduce 10 percent import duty on sugar and flood the market with foodstuffs.
THE NEWS
- The government plans to float investment bonds for overseas Pakistanis to make local capital markets more vibrant.
- The Central Board of Revenue has scaled down revenue target for 1996-97 (July-June) to 290 billion rupees from 305 billion.
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif has asked the provincial chief ministers to make new legislation to curb sectarian violence.
- Former prime minister Benazir Bhutto left for the United States on Sunday and is likely to return on May 18.
- Foreign Minister Gohar Ayub said the government is keen to develop friendly relations with the Soviet Union.
THE NATION
- The government has decided to abolish 10 percent import duty on sugar to guard against any future shortages.
